## Overview

The concentration in the air is advanced by a numerical scheme, chosen as the algorithm passed
to `solve`: implicit Euler (`EulerBackward`, the AeoLiS default), `CrankNicolson`, or
explicit Euler (`EulerForward`, with the time step limited by the CFL number). Inside a
scheme the transport solver is `Trunk` (an upwind discretisation solved as a sparse linear
system), `Pieter` (a finite-volume form with fluxes on cell faces) or `SteadyState` (an
upwind sweep that finds the equilibrium with the current wind). The sparse systems are solved
with LinearSolve.jl, so any of its sparse factorizations can be used.

```{julia}
#| output: false
ENV["GKSwstype"] = "100"
using Aeolis
using LinearSolve
using Plots
```

## A test problem

A beach with a varying wind, so that the concentration is not always in equilibrium:

```{julia}
x = collect(0.0:1.0:100.0)
t = 0.0:600.0:86400.0
wind = hcat(t, 8 .+ 6 .* sin.(t ./ 3000.0) .^ 2, fill(270.0, length(t)))
p = AeolisParameters(; xgrid_file=x, bed_file=fill(1.0, length(x)), wind_file=wind,
                     grain_size=0.0003, dt=300.0, tstop=6 * 3600.0, output_times=1800.0,
                     output_vars=[:zb, :qs], CFL=1.0)
prob = AeolisProblem(p)
```

## Schemes and solvers

```{julia}
algs = ["EulerBackward(Trunk())" => EulerBackward(Trunk()),
        "CrankNicolson(Trunk())" => CrankNicolson(Trunk()),
        "EulerForward(Trunk())" => EulerForward(Trunk()),
        "EulerBackward(Pieter())" => EulerBackward(Pieter()),
        "EulerBackward(SteadyState())" => EulerBackward(SteadyState())]
sols = Dict(name => solve(prob, alg) for (name, alg) in algs)
plt = plot(; xlabel="time (h)", ylabel="flux at x = 99 m (kg/m/s)", legend=:topleft)
for (name, _) in algs
    s = sols[name]
    plot!(plt, s.t ./ 3600, transect(s, :qs)[end - 1, 1, :]; lw=2, label=name)
end
plt
```

The explicit scheme takes many more steps, since the CFL number limits its time step to the
time the wind takes to cross a cell; the solution statistics count the time steps and the
matrix solves:

```{julia}
[(name, get(sols[name].stats, :time, 0), get(sols[name].stats, :matrixsolve, 0))
 for (name, _) in algs]
```

The bed level after six hours differs by less than a millimetre between the time-dependent
schemes; the steady-state solver, which ignores the time the concentration takes to adjust,
differs by a few millimetres:

```{julia}
ref = transect(sols["EulerBackward(Trunk())"], :zb)[:, end]
[(name, maximum(abs.(transect(sols[name], :zb)[:, end] .- ref))) for (name, _) in algs]
```

## Linear solvers

The trunk and pieter solvers assemble one sparse matrix per fraction and time step and solve
it repeatedly while the fraction weights are adjusted to the available sediment; the
factorization is reused across these solves. A LinearSolve.jl algorithm can be given with
`linsolve`:

```{julia}
for lin in (nothing, KLUFactorization(), UMFPACKFactorization())
    s = solve(prob, EulerBackward(Trunk(); linsolve=lin))
    d = maximum(abs.(transect(s, :zb)[:, end] .- ref))
    println(rpad(string(something(lin, "default")), 30), " max difference ", d)
end
```
